Laura — quick technical-commercial note from my side: 

- Pilot scope: recommend Dedicated burst pool with autoscale up to 1.5x baseline for first 90 days. That lets you validate the new product traffic while keeping initial commit modest.
- Commercial suggestion: apply a temporary 10% rebate on incremental usage above baseline for the pilot quarter (rebate applied as invoice credit). This reduces lift risk while keeping us aligned on utilization.
- Price hold: we can lock the existing committed rate for a 90-day guaranteed window. Procurement asked about 180 days — we can extend to 180 days if the customer accepts a small step-down protection (i.e., guaranteed rate for committed baseline + conditional review at day 90).

I've attached a usage snapshot and a draft MPA terms doc with the staged uplift language. If legal wants firm contract language, I can put together redline suggestions.

Thanks Ben — that approach is close to what Procurement is looking for. A couple of clarifications and asks from legal/procurement: 

- Procurement preference is to lock pricing for 180 days (not conditional). They typically operate with a 180-day review window for suppliers when evaluating multi-quarter pilots.
- The rebate needs to be applied as a credit on invoices (not a rebate check) and should be visible in billing detail.
- We need an explicit milestone credit if we convert to a committed tier after the pilot. Target is a one-time conversion credit applied to the final invoice after the milestone is verified.

Laura — appreciate the clarity from procurement. Below is a commercial proposal we can circulate as a one-page commercial term sheet and then fold into the MPA redline: 

1) Temporary price hold: 180 days from effective date. We will lock the committed baseline rate for the 180-day window (no unilateral price increases for that baseline).

2) Pilot uplift: Dedicated burst pool with autoscale up to 1.5x baseline for first 90 days. Usage beyond baseline billed at published incremental rate during the pilot.

3) Pilot rebate: 10% invoice credit applied to incremental usage above baseline during the pilot quarter (applied monthly to invoices as a credit line item).

4) Conversion/milestone credit: one-time $25,000 credit applied to invoice after Helios achieves sustained 1.2x baseline throughput for 30 consecutive days within the first 90 days. Proof to be mutually agreed (billing metrics + production traffic logs).

5) Conditional extension: after 90 days, we will meet to review pilot results. If Helios elects to convert to a committed tier within the 180-day hold window, we will apply the conversion credit and confirm new commit pricing per the MPA. If not, pricing reverts to the committed baseline + published rates.

Next steps: I will put the one-page commercial term sheet into a PDF and create a HubSpot deal record (HL-2027-045). Ben will prepare a redline of the MPA with the staged uplift and credit language. Marissa and I can coordinate legal/finance review.
